results.name: Bench Pull-Ups
instructions: Position yourself under a pull-up bar with one foot placed on a bench for support.
Grip the pull-up bar with both hands, using an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Pull your chest towards the bar, engaging your back and arm muscles.
Lower yourself back down to the starting position in a controlled manner, keeping your core engaged.
tips: Ensure the bench is stable and your supporting foot is firmly placed to maintain balance.
Focus on using your back muscles to pull yourself up rather than relying solely on your arms.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
results.description: Bench Pull-Ups is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Let the barbell hang directly in front of you with your arms fully extended. Pull the barbell towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders or lower back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize upper back engagement.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
results.description: Bent Over Barbell Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Bent Over Row Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles of a resistance band anchored under your feet. Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in your knees to bring your torso almost parallel to the floor.
Start with your arms extended towards the floor, holding the band with your palms facing each other.
Pull the handles of the band towards your hips by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arms back towards the floor. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize back engagement and minimize shoulder involvement.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Bent Over Row Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Bent-Over Row With Bar
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Let the bar hang directly in front of you with your arms fully extended. Pull the bar towards your abdomen by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize upper back engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
results.description: Bent-Over Row With Bar is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Bodyweight Muscle-Up
instructions: Start by hanging from a bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Pull yourself up explosively, transitioning from a pull-up to a dip position above the bar.
Push your body up until your arms are fully extended above the bar.
Lower yourself back down to the starting hanging position in a controlled manner. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core and maintain a straight body line to ensure proper form.
Use an explosive pull-up motion to help transition from below the bar to above the bar.
Focus on a controlled descent to avoid straining your muscles and joints.
results.description: Bodyweight Muscle-Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Triceps.

results.name: Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown
instructions: Sit at a cable pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip, your arms fully extended overhead.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, bringing your elbows down and back.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with your arms fully extended overhead. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and with control.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on the contraction of your back muscles as you pull the bar down.
results.description: Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Cable Bent Over Reverse Grip Row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley on a cable machine. Stand facing the machine and grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips to form a 90 degree angle with your upper body, keeping your knees slightly bent. Let your arms extend with the cable, holding the bar.
Pull the bar towards your lower abdomen, bringing your elbows backwards.
Slowly extend the bar back to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you pull the bar towards you and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body; focus on isolating the back muscles.
results.description: Cable Bent Over Reverse Grip Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Bent Over Row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley on a cable machine. Stand facing the machine and grasp the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips to form a 90 degree angle with your upper body, keeping your knees slightly bent. Let your arms extend with the cable, holding the bar.
Pull the bar towards your lower abdomen, bringing your elbows backwards.
Slowly extend the bar back to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you pull the bar towards you and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body; focus on isolating the back muscles.
results.description: Cable Bent Over Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Close Grip Front Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar attached to the machine with your arms fully extended above you, hands closer than shoulder-width and palms facing forward.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, bringing your elbows down and back while slightly leaning back.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position with your arms fully extended overhead.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control.
Exhale as you pull the handle down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your chest stays up and your shoulders down to avoid rounding your back.
results.description: Cable Close Grip Front Lat Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Cable Lat Prayer
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine and hold the handles overhead with your arms fully extended. Hinge at your hips and lean forward until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the handles downward in an arc toward your thighs.
Pause briefly while squeezing your lats at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise.
Hinge at your hips and maintain a neutral spine.
Control the movement and avoid using momentum.
Inhale as you return the handles overhead and exhale as you pull them downward.
results.description: Cable Lat Prayer is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.
